frontmatter.title: Data Analysis Methods at a Glance

children.value: This page is the reference for all analyses of the behavioural and questionnaire data: what is measured, which models are fitted, how they are coded and tested, which script runs them and where the results are. The task is described in
, the computational model and its fitting in
Fitting the Models to Participant Data
, and the commands that run everything in
is the draft of the manuscript’s methods; this page gives the same content as an overview.

Sections 1 to 3 define the data, the measures and the conventions that hold for every model. Section 4 lists the analyses, grouped by question, each with its unit of analysis, outcome, model, script and the page with its results. Section 5 maps the names used in code, outputs and manuscript draft. Section 6 lists where the outputs are.
86 with behavioural data (run 13_11); 85 with questionnaires (84 for STICSA state and OCI)
None (no rules given): 31; Partial (rules mentioned): 33; Full (structure explained): 22 (21 with questionnaires)

9 episodes, 171 to 188 trials (median 181; 20 trial schedules); two colour cues per episode (cue B = cue A + 70°); about 9 % oddballs and 10 % omissions (attack not shown); 8 transitions per participant

Five focal questionnaires enter every questionnaire model: STICSA state and STICSA trait (anxiety), IU (intolerance of uncertainty, IUS-18), BDI (BDI-II, depressive symptoms) and OCI (OCI-R, obsessive-compulsive symptoms). Five further questionnaires are analysed in some places and corrected separately: PCL-5, ACE, SIAS, ERS, EAT. Total scores are used; in every model they are z-scored within the participants of that analysis.
After each episode, six ratings from 0 to 100: valence, arousal, anxiety, stress, frustration, fatigue.
